replace.vision_ground: Retrieve and present up to three inspectable candidate regions for one short text description in the current native-resolution RGB-D observation. Use when: the task names an object or part and the Agent should reduce the scene-level visual search space before making its own semantic identity decision. Effect: read-only with respect to the world and creates separate observation-bound target_ref artifacts for every returned candidate; the service proposes regions but the Agent remains the selection authority. Returns: zero to three ranked candidates with target_ref, backend-local score, bounding box and visible-depth summary, followed by image 0 as the numbered full-scene overview and one labelled 1024x800 raw/mask candidate card per result in T0/T1/T2 order; compare the enlarged raw appearances and select the intended target_ref yourself. Does not: make a black-box semantic decision, certify that any candidate is the named object, add sensor resolution, treat backend score as calibrated probability, expose object ground truth, or prove reachability or grasp success. On error: rephrase the visible description to obtain a better candidate set, switch current camera, inspect with observe, or use point-based vision_segment for an instance the Agent can already identify. Selection check: compare the requested task referent with every candidate crop and the original view; rank 0 and a high score do not authenticate identity. Separate an instance hypothesis from an observed property. Failed grasping is not evidence that the intended object is static or that a different object is the target. Revise a mistaken association when the visible evidence contradicts it. Boundary and mask/depth diagnostics describe observability, not semantic truth.
